summary: Lesotho waives visas for SADC citizens and a broad list of Commonwealth and Western European nationalities — including the US, UK and Ireland — typically for up to 90 days, or 30 days for SADC citizens. Everyone else needs a visa before travel from a Lesotho embassy or high commission: the former eVisa site is no longer a safe route.

passportValidity.text: Your passport must be valid for at least 90 days after the date you arrive in Lesotho, and have at least 4 blank pages: Lesotho stamps it, and so does South Africa on the way in and out.

source.name: UK Foreign Office — Lesotho entry requirements
UK Foreign Office — Lesotho entry requirements

travelInsurance.text: Visa applicants must submit proof of medical insurance with the application. Visa-free visitors are not asked for it, but it is strongly recommended — healthcare in the highlands is very limited and serious cases are evacuated to South Africa.

source.name: Government of Lesotho — Service charter: Issuance of entry visa

onwardTicket.text: Onward tickets are not systematically checked at the land borders; airlines flying into Maseru may ask for a return or onward booking.

source.name: UK Foreign Office — Lesotho entry requirements

proofOfFunds.text: Tourist visa applicants must submit three months of bank statements or a valid debit or credit card with enough funds for the stay; visitors invited by a sponsor show statements of at least M10,000. No amount is published for visa-free arrivals.

source.name: Government of Lesotho — Service charter: Issuance of entry visa

currencyLimits.text: Declare cash or travellers cheques in any currency worth 25,000 maloti or more, or the money can be seized when you leave and you can be fined. The loti is pegged 1:1 to the South African rand, and both are accepted throughout Lesotho.

source.name: UK Foreign Office — Lesotho entry requirements

notes: Lesotho is in the Southern African Customs Union — goods bought in South Africa generally cross without duty, but commercial quantities must be declared.

payments.text: Cards are accepted at hotels, lodges and larger shops in Maseru, but most of the country runs on cash. South African rand are accepted everywhere at 1:1 alongside the loti. Carry small notes for rural areas.

safety.text: Lesotho is generally welcoming and rural areas are calm; petty crime and occasional robberies occur in Maseru, so avoid walking alone after dark. In practice the bigger risks are mountain roads, altitude and fast-changing weather.

source.name: UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office — Lesotho travel advice

bestTimeToVisit.text: March to May and September to November bring mild, clear weather for hiking and pony trekking. Summer (December–February) is green but stormy; June to August is cold with snow on the high passes, and skiing at Afriski.

idp.text: Lesotho is a party to the 1949 Geneva Convention on Road Traffic but not to the 1968 Vienna one, so the International Driving Permit it is bound to recognize is the 1949 Geneva version. A permit issued under the 1968 Vienna Convention carries no treaty obligation here.

driving.text: Lesotho is a party to the 1949 Geneva Convention on Road Traffic but not to the 1968 Vienna one, so the International Driving Permit it is bound to recognize is the 1949 Geneva version. A permit issued under the 1968 Vienna Convention carries no treaty obligation here. Whether a permit is required in addition to a national license, and for how long a foreign license may be used, are set by national road law and have not been checked for Lesotho yet.

tips.text: The entire country lies above 1,400 m — the highest lowest point of any nation. Mountain weather changes fast: pack warm layers even in summer and expect snow and icy passes from June to August.

The famous Sani Pass crossing from South Africa requires a 4x4 — ordinary cars are not allowed up the pass and many South African rental contracts exclude it. Check your rental terms before planning the route.
South African rand are accepted everywhere at 1:1 with the loti, but maloti cannot be spent back in South Africa — change or spend them before you leave.
Most land border posts with South Africa close in the evening — many by 20:00 or earlier. Maseru Bridge is the main 24-hour crossing; check the hours of smaller posts like Sani Pass before traveling.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Lesotho?
faq.answer: Citizens of SADC countries and of a broad list of Commonwealth and Western European states — including the US, UK, Ireland and Germany — enter Lesotho visa-free, typically for up to 90 days (SADC citizens are usually admitted for 30 days per entry). Other nationalities need a visa before travel, from a Lesotho embassy or high commission.

faq.question: Can I visit Lesotho on a day trip from South Africa?
faq.answer: Yes — day trips via Sani Pass, Maseru Bridge or the smaller posts are common. You go through full passport control both ways, so make sure your South African visa or entry allowance permits re-entry, and remember Sani Pass requires a 4x4.

faq.question: Can I extend my stay in Lesotho?
faq.answer: Yes. Before your current permission expires, complete a 90-day temporary permit extension form and take it to the Visa Application Centre in the Manthabiseng Convention Centre, Maseru. Your passport must be valid for the extension period, and overstaying brings detention and weekly fines.

faq.question: Can I still apply for a Lesotho visa online?
faq.answer: Not safely. The former eVisa address, evisalesotho.com, has served a Turkish gambling site since at least February 2025, and Home Affairs now links to a notice that online visa applications are suspended. Apply at a Lesotho embassy or high commission, and do not pay any site claiming to be the Lesotho eVisa until the government publishes a new address.

faq.question: Do I need a yellow fever certificate for Lesotho?
faq.answer: Lesotho itself does not require one (WHO). But South Africa, which you cross on every overland route and usually fly through, requires a certificate from travellers aged 1 or over arriving from a country with risk of yellow fever transmission or after more than 12 hours' transit in one — so if that applies to you, carry it.
